title: Vanishing above m gives the m-pseudo-coherent base case
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $m$ be an integer, and let $D(R)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $R$-modules. Call an object $C$ of $D(R)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules and a morphism $E^\bullet\to C$ in $D(R)$ inducing isomorphisms $H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C)$ for $i>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C)$. If $H^i(C)=0$ for every $i\ge m$, then $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.66.5 (Tag 064W), base case of the m-pseudo-coherence induction

proof.text: Take the bounded complex $E^\bullet=0$ of finite free $R$-modules and its zero morphism to $C$ in $D(R)$. For every $i>m$, the hypothesis gives $H^i(C)=0$, so $H^i(E^\bullet)=0\to H^i(C)$ is an isomorphism. In degree $m$, the same hypothesis gives $H^m(C)=0$, so $H^m(E^\bullet)=0\to H^m(C)$ is surjective. Thus this morphism witnesses that $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent (Stacks, More on Algebra, Tag 064W, part (1)).
